'''Bjarni Valdimar Tryggvason''' (September 21, 1945 – April 5, 2022) was an Icelandic-born Canadian engineer and a [[National Research Council (Canada)|NRC]]/[[CSA astronaut]]. He served as a [[Payload Specialist]] on [[Space Shuttle]] mission [[STS-85]] in 1997, a nearly 12-day mission to study changes in the [[Earth's atmosphere]]. Bjarni is the first, and {{as of|2024|lc=y}}, only Canadian astronaut of Icelandic birth.

== Early life ==
Tryggvason was born in [[Reykjavík]] on September 21, 1945.<ref name="CSA bio">{{cite web|title=Biography of Bjarni Tryggvason|url=https://asc-csa.gc.ca/eng/astronauts/canadian/former/bio-bjarni-tryggvason.asp|date=April 6, 2022|access-date=April 9, 2022|publisher=Canadian Space Agency|location=Longueuil|archive-date=April 6, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406212034/https://asc-csa.gc.ca/eng/astronauts/canadian/former/bio-bjarni-tryggvason.asp|url-status=live}}</ref> He moved to Canada with his parents when he was eight,<ref name=mbl>{{cite news |url=https://www.mbl.is/frettir/innlent/2022/04/06/bjarni_geimfari_latinn/ |title=Bjarni geimfari látinn |newspaper=Morgunblaðið |date=April 6, 2022 |language=is |access-date=April 7, 2022 |archive-date=April 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406224924/https://www.mbl.is/frettir/innlent/2022/04/06/bjarni_geimfari_latinn/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and grew up in [[Vancouver|Vancouver, British Columbia]]. After attending high school in [[Richmond, British Columbia]], he obtained a B.A.Sc. degree in [[engineering physics]] from the [[University of British Columbia]] in 1972, and subsequently studied at the postgraduate level in engineering with specialization in [[applied mathematics]] and [[fluid dynamics]] at the [[University of Western Ontario]].<ref name = "NASA bio"/>

== Academic career  ==
Tryggvason worked as a [[meteorologist]] with the [[cloud physics]] group at the [[Atmospheric Environment Service]] in [[Toronto]] in 1972 and 1973. In 1974, he joined the University of Western Ontario to work as a research associate at the Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel Laboratory working on projects involving rigid and [[aeroelasticity|aero-elastic]] model studies of wind effects on structures.<ref name = "NASA bio"/> In 1987, he was a guest research associate at [[Kyoto University]], Japan. This was followed by a similar position at [[James Cook University]] in [[Townsville, Queensland|Townsville]], Australia. In late 1979, he returned to the University of Western Ontario as a lecturer in applied mathematics.<ref name = "NASA bio"/>

In 1982, Tryggvason joined the Low Speed Aerodynamics Laboratory at the [[United States National Research Council|National Research Council]] (NRC) in [[Ottawa]]. He became part of the NRC team assembled to study the sinking of the ''[[Ocean Ranger]]'' oil rig in support of the Royal Commission investigation. He designed and led the aerodynamics tests, which established the wind loads acting on the rig. Between 1981 and 1992, he was also a part-time lecturer at the [[University of Ottawa]] and [[Carleton University]], teaching graduate courses on [[structural dynamics]] and [[random vibration]]s.<ref name = "NASA bio"/>

Tryggvason had about 4,000 hours of flight experience, held an Airline Transport Rating and had experience as a [[flight instructor]]. He was active in [[Aerobatic maneuver|aerobatic flight]] and once qualified as captain in the [[Canadair CT-114 Tutor|Tutor]] jet trainer with the [[Royal Canadian Air Force]].<ref name="NASA bio">{{cite web |url=http://www.jsc.nasa.gov/Bios/htmlbios/tryggvas.html |title=BJARNI V. TRYGGVASON ASTRONAUT, CANADIAN SPACE AGENCY |publisher=[[NASA]] |work=Biographical Data |date=August 2006 |access-date=February 23, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525193350/http://www.jsc.nasa.gov/Bios/htmlbios/tryggvas.html |archive-date=May 25, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== CSA career ==
Tryggvason was one of the six Canadian astronauts selected in December 1983, and was the first Canadian astronaut born in Iceland.<ref name=mbl/> He was back-up [[Payload Specialist]] to [[Steven MacLean (astronaut)|Steven MacLean]] for the CANEX-2 set of experiments which flew on Mission [[STS-52]], October 22 to November 1, 1992. He was the Project Engineer for the design of the SVS target spacecraft which was deployed during that mission.<ref name = "NASA bio"/>

He was the principal investigator in the development of the Large Motion Isolation Mount, which has flown numerous times on the [[NASA]] [[Boeing KC-135]] and [[Douglas DC-9|DC-9]] aircraft, for the Microgravity vibration Isolation Mount (MIM), which operated on the Russian [[Mir space station]] from April 1996 until January 1998, and for the MIM-2, which flew on [[STS-85]] in August 1997. The MIM was used on the Mir to support several Canadian and US experiments in material science and fluid physics.<ref name = "NASA bio"/>

Tryggvason served as a payload specialist on [[STS-85]] (August 7–19, 1997), a 12-day mission to study changes in the Earth's atmosphere. During the flight, his primary role was testing MIM-2 and performing fluid dynamics experiments designed to examine sensitivity to spacecraft vibrations. This work was directed at developing better understanding of the need for systems such as the MIM on the [[International Space Station]] (ISS) and on the effect of vibrations on the many experiments to be performed on the ISS. The mission was accomplished in 189 Earth orbits, traveling 4.7 million miles in 284 hours and 28 minutes.<ref name = "NASA bio"/>

In August 1998, Tryggvason became part of [[NASA Astronaut Group 17]]. Training consisted of two years of physical and academic training relating to future missions. The class was the first group of astronauts to be trained as both mission specialist for the [[Space Shuttle]] and as potential crewmembers for the ISS. He was initially assigned as a [[Shuttle Avionics Integration Laboratory]] (SAIL) crew representative. SAIL is used to test, check out, and verify Shuttle flight software prior to use. He also supported integrated simulations on the ISS Training Facility. This facility is used for ISS crew training as well as in support of training the ISS Mission Control team.<ref name = "NASA bio"/>

== Post-CSA career ==
[[File:Silver Dart Centenary 2009 201.jpg|thumb|right|Bjarni Tryggvason and son Michael talking to the crowd after completing five flights on the Silver Dart replica on February 22, 2009]]

Tryggvason retired from the [[Canadian Space Agency]] in June 2008.<ref>{{cite news | agency=[[Canadian Press]] | url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/science/canadian-astronaut-bjarni-tryggvason-to-retire-1.733025 | title=Canadian astronaut Bjarni Tryggvason to retire | publisher=[[The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] | date=May 1, 2008 | access-date=February 23, 2009 | url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090608235523/http://www.cbc.ca/news/story/2008/05/01/tech-bjarni-retire.html | archive-date=June 8, 2009}}</ref> He returned to teaching at the [[University of Western Ontario]].<ref>{{cite news | agency=[[Canadian Press]] | url=https://www.thestar.com/article/583699 | title=Shuttle astronaut flies replica of 1909 Silver Dart |work=The Toronto Star | date=February 6, 2009 | access-date=February 23, 2009 | last=Perkel | first=Colin | location=Hamilton, Ontario |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090609004344/http://www.thestar.com/article/583699 | archive-date=June 9, 2009}}</ref> He also taught at the [[International Test Pilots School]] in [[London, Ontario]], and continued to serve as a test pilot.<ref name=Petty>{{cite news|title=Man on a Mission|url=https://trekmagazine.alumni.ubc.ca/2018/fall-2018/features/man-on-a-mission|first=Chris|last=Petty|date=November 27, 2018|access-date=April 9, 2022|magazine=TREK|publisher=University of British Columbia|archive-date=April 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416022119/https://trekmagazine.alumni.ubc.ca/2018/fall-2018/features/man-on-a-mission|url-status=live}}</ref>

On February 22, 2009, Tryggvason piloted a replica of [[Alexander Graham Bell]]'s [[AEA Silver Dart|Silver Dart]], from the ice on Baddeck Bay, [[Cape Breton Island]], [[Nova Scotia]]. The flight commemorated the centennial of the first flight in Canada and the British Empire. Due to poor weather conditions expected on the next day, the flight occurred one day before the actual centenary of the original Silver Dart's flight.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/silver-dart-replica-takes-flight-in-nova-scotia-1.834833 | title=Silver Dart replica takes flight in Nova Scotia | work=CBC News | date=February 22, 2009 | access-date=May 4, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130829001210/http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/story/2009/02/22/silver-dart.html | archive-date=August 29, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Tryggvason had two children.<ref name="CSA bio"/>  His son also went into aviation as a [[commercial pilot]], while his daughter was a [[veterinarian]].<ref name=Petty/> Tryggvason died on April 5, 2022, at the age of 76.<ref name="CP obit">{{cite news|title=Former Canadian astronaut Bjarni Tryggvason dead at 76|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/former-canadian-astronaut-bjarni-tryggvason-dead-1.6410863|date=April 6, 2022|access-date=April 9, 2022|publisher=CBC News|agency=The Canadian Press|archive-date=April 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220409072746/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/former-canadian-astronaut-bjarni-tryggvason-dead-1.6410863|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="CSA obit">{{cite news|title=The Canadian Space Agency remembers Bjarni Tryggvason|url=https://www.canada.ca/en/space-agency/news/2022/04/the-canadian-space-agency-remembers-bjarni-tryggvason.html|date=April 6, 2022|access-date=April 9, 2022|publisher=Canadian Space Agency|location=Longueuil|archive-date=April 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220409064740/https://www.canada.ca/en/space-agency/news/2022/04/the-canadian-space-agency-remembers-bjarni-tryggvason.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Honors and affiliations==

Tryggvason was a member of the [[Canadian Aeronautics and Space Institute]]. He was awarded an honorary [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] degree from the [[University of Western Ontario]] in 1998,<ref>[https://www.uwo.ca/univsec/pdf/senate/minutes/1998/r9809hdg.html Report of the Honorary Degrees Committee] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200821083352/https://www.uwo.ca/univsec/pdf/senate/minutes/1998/r9809hdg.html |date=August 21, 2020 }} - website of the University of Western Ontario</ref> an honorary [[Doctor of Technology|Dr. Techn.]] degree from the [[University of Iceland]] in 2000,<ref name = "NASA bio"/><ref>[https://english.hi.is/university/honorary_degrees#Honorary_degree_recipients_2000-2009 Honorary Degrees: Honorary degree recipients 2000-2009] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210412164126/https://english.hi.is/university/honorary_degrees#Honorary_degree_recipients_2000-2009 |date=April 12, 2021 }} - website of the University of Iceland</ref> and an honorary [[Doctor of Engineering|D.Eng.]] degree from the [[University of Victoria]] in 2005.<ref>[https://www.uvic.ca/news/topics/2005+uvic-confers-honorary-degrees+media-release Astronaut-Scientist, Eco-Forester to Receive Honorary Degrees] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180714223618/https://www.uvic.ca/news/topics/2005+uvic-confers-honorary-degrees+media-release |date=July 14, 2018 }} - website of the University of Victoria</ref> He was furthermore awarded the [[NASA Space Flight Medal]] in 1997, the Innovators Award of the [[Canadian Space Agency]] in 2004, and the Knight's Cross of the Icelandic [[Order of the Falcon]] in 2000.<ref name = "NASA bio"/><ref name="CSA obit"/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://timarit.is/page/1974891#page/n5/mode/2up |title=13 sæmdir fálkaorðunni |newspaper=Morgunblaðið |date=August 5, 2000 |language=is |access-date=April 11, 2022 |archive-date=April 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220411214305/https://timarit.is/page/1974891#page/n5/mode/2up |url-status=live }}</ref>
